key_insight: An agent can reuse and refine an experimental strategy across different quantum processors, enabling the same quantum task to be completed despite device-specific differences and drift.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path toward scalable quantum-lab automation, where human operators handle setup while an agent adapts measurements and procedures across heterogeneous hardware.
method: Developed an agent-assisted workflow on one three-qubit NMR processor and transferred it sequentially to four others.
The agent evaluated experimental evidence, chose follow-up measurements, and adapted procedures while operators performed instrument preparation and physical intervention.
Each deployment combined device-specific calibration, control-pulse optimization, and measurement for three-qubit Grover state preparation.
evidence_signal: Across four transferred deployments, the reconstructed dominant eigenstates showed marked-state populations from 0.910 to 0.959, with relative deviations below 3.8% from the ideal 0.945.
watch_item: The approach still depends on human operator intervention and device-specific calibration, so real-world scaling may be constrained by hardware drift and the need for expert oversight.
paper_title: Agent-assisted experimental strategy transfer across quantum processors
